title: Task decomposition for robot manipulation
reading: The slide presents the MOKA pipeline as an example of using a vision-language model to decompose a natural-language manipulation instruction into subtasks and then into concrete robot motions. A photo of a Franka arm on a cluttered table sits alongside a multi-stage pipeline figure showing text prompts, VLM responses, segmentation, mark-based visual prompting and generated motion. Attribution is to Liu et al., MOKA: Open-World Robotic Manipulation through Mark-Based Visual Prompting, 2024.

visuals.description: Franka Emika robot arm with wrist camera above a table holding eyeglasses, a brush/broom, a snack package and a yellow case; a shaded orange region marks the camera's field of view.
visuals.assertion: The real-world setup corresponds to the instruction about wiping trash and moving eyeglasses into a case.

visuals.description: Two-stage pipeline: a user message ('Use the broom to wipe the trash to the right side of the table after moving the eyeglasses into the case.') plus image goes to a VLM for high-level reasoning with a text prompt asking to decompose the task into subtasks; the response is a JSON subtask with instruction, object_inhand 'broom', object_unattached 'trash', motion_direction 'to the right'. Segmentation masks are drawn on the input image, then a grid-marked image serves as a visual prompt to a second VLM for low-level reasoning, whose response gives affordance keypoints (grasp_keypoint P5, function_keypoint P3, target_keypoint Q1, pre/post_contact_tile c4/e4), producing a generated motion trajectory overlaid on the scene.
visuals.assertion: Manipulation can be solved by a VLM first decomposing language into structured subtasks, then selecting keypoints/waypoints on a marked image to yield executable motions.

concepts.name: Task decomposition into subtasks
concepts.why_it_matters: Turns a long-horizon language command into tractable steps a policy can execute.

concepts.name: Mark-based visual prompting
concepts.why_it_matters: Overlaying grids and candidate keypoints lets a VLM output spatially grounded actions.

concepts.name: Affordance keypoints and waypoints
concepts.why_it_matters: Provide the interface between VLM output and low-level motion generation.

concepts.why_it_matters: Core reasoning engine at both hierarchy levels.
